info: Every mission follows: Explore → Story → Decision → Consequence → Reflection → Reward. Steps run in order unless a choice or step has "next".
reflectionReasons: I wanted to be fair and polite.
It felt like the easiest choice.

missions.title: The Locked Garden
missions.summary: Mary Lennox arrives at Misselthwaite Manor, lonely and cross. A robin leads her to a buried key, and she learns that the garden was locked out of sadness.
missions.stageText: Fresh grass returns to the garden.

steps.text: Misselthwaite Manor, Yorkshire. Mary Lennox has just arrived from India. The house has a hundred rooms, and most of them are locked. Outside, the wind blows across the moor.

steps.speaker: mary
steps.text: Nobody here plays with me. Everyone just tells me to keep out of the way.
Martha, the young housemaid, tells Mary a secret: one garden has been locked for ten years. When Mrs. Craven died, Mr. Craven locked the door and buried the key.

steps.speaker: ben
steps.text: Hmph. Children shouldn't go poking about. That garden's none of your business.

steps.speaker: mary
steps.prompt: Ben Weatherstaff, the old gardener, looks grumpy. Mary really wants to know about the garden. What should she do?

options.text: Demand: “Tell me where the door is!”
options.feedback: Think about how Ben might feel. The garden holds a sad memory for him.

reaction.speaker: ben
reaction.text: I'll tell thee nothing. Off with you!

options.text: Ask Ben about the little robin he is talking to.
options.feedback: Starting with what Ben loves showed respect and kindness.

reaction.speaker: ben
reaction.text: That robin? He's my only friend, he is. Lonely, like me.

options.text: Gently ask him why the garden was locked, and listen.
options.feedback: This choice showed understanding.

reaction.speaker: ben
reaction.text: She loved that garden, the mistress did. It's been shut up ever since.

options.text: Give up and go back inside alone.
options.feedback: Sometimes a gentle question can open a door. What could Mary ask?

reaction.speaker: mary
reaction.text: …Nobody ever tells me anything.

steps.book: Mary arrives in a strange new house. Nobody talks to her, and she feels lonely and cross.
steps.today: A new student joins your class in the middle of the year and eats lunch alone.

steps.text: The robin hops along the old wall and scratches at the soil. Help Mary find what is hidden near the Old Tree.
Under the robin's feet, Mary finds an old rusty key! Later, the wind lifts the ivy on the wall and shows a hidden door.

steps.speaker: mary
steps.prompt: Martha says Mr. Craven still can't bear to think about the garden. What does Mary think about him?

options.text: “He's just a mean, unfriendly man.”
options.feedback: Think about why someone might lock away something they once loved.

reaction.speaker: martha
reaction.text: He's not mean, Miss. He's just very, very sad.

options.text: “The garden holds sad memories. I should be gentle with it.”
options.feedback: This choice showed understanding.

reaction.speaker: martha
reaction.text: Eh, that's a kind way to think, Miss Mary.

options.text: “I'll look after the garden, so something good can grow from the sadness.”
options.feedback: Wanting to turn sadness into something good showed compassion.

reaction.speaker: martha
reaction.text: Mother says a garden is good medicine for a sad heart.

options.text: “His feelings don't matter. I found the key.”
options.feedback: How might Mr. Craven feel if he knew? Try to see it from his side.

reaction.speaker: martha
reaction.text: Oh, Miss… please be careful.

missions.title: Mary's Choice
missions.summary: Mary learns that the way she speaks to Martha matters. Kindness from Martha's family softens her, and she chooses whether to share her secret garden.
missions.stageText: The first flowers open in the garden.

steps.text: The rose garden is grey and tangled. Mary remembers her first morning at the manor, when Martha opened the curtains and started chatting in her strong Yorkshire voice.

steps.speaker: martha
steps.text: Good mornin', Miss! Look at that moor out there. Isn't it grand? Eat your porridge, now.
In India, Mary's servants never spoke to her like that. Mary feels cross and confused. This is a branching story — each choice changes what happens next.

steps.speaker: mary
steps.prompt: What Should Mary Do? Martha is friendly, but Mary is used to giving orders.

options.text: Order Martha to be quiet and leave.
options.feedback: How do you think Martha felt? Watch what happens next.

reaction.speaker: martha
reaction.text: Eh… I'm sorry, Miss. I only wanted to be friendly.

options.text: Ask Martha about her family on the moor.
options.feedback: Showing interest in Martha's life showed understanding.

reaction.speaker: martha
reaction.text: There's twelve of us at home! Our Dickon can charm any animal on the moor.

options.text: Say thank you for the breakfast.
options.feedback: A simple thank-you showed respect.

reaction.speaker: martha
reaction.text: Well! You're welcome, Miss. My, that's nice to hear.

steps.text: Martha's smile fades. Mary feels a strange, uncomfortable feeling inside. It is the first time she has wondered how someone else feels.

steps.speaker: mary
steps.prompt: Martha is quietly folding the blankets. What should Mary do now?

options.text: Say sorry to Martha.
options.feedback: Saying sorry showed respect. It is never too late to change your words.

reaction.speaker: martha
reaction.text: Bless you, Miss. That's all right, then.

options.text: Pretend nothing happened.
options.feedback: Think about how Martha might feel if nobody mentions it.

reaction.speaker: martha
reaction.text: …I'll be going, then, Miss.

options.text: Ask Martha to tell her about the moor.
options.feedback: Starting a friendly conversation is a kind way to repair things.

reaction.speaker: martha
reaction.text: Oh, the moor's lovely in spring, Miss! All gorse and heather.

steps.text: Martha's mother sends Mary a skipping rope. She bought it with her own small savings, even though the family is poor.

steps.speaker: mary
steps.prompt: Mary has never received a present like this before. How should she respond?

options.text: Say it's a cheap toy.
options.feedback: Think about what this gift cost Martha's family.

reaction.speaker: martha
reaction.text: Mother did her best, Miss.

options.text: Thank Martha and her mother warmly.
options.feedback: This choice showed kindness.

reaction.speaker: martha
reaction.text: Mother'll be that pleased, Miss!

options.text: Ask how she could do something kind for them in return.
options.feedback: Wanting to give back showed caring.

reaction.speaker: martha
reaction.text: You could come and meet Dickon one day. He'd like that.

steps.text: Weeks later, Mary stands in the secret garden. The roses look dead. She wants to keep the garden secret forever — but Dickon knows how to make things grow.

steps.speaker: mary
steps.prompt: Should Mary share her secret garden with Dickon?

options.text: Keep it to herself. It's hers alone.
options.feedback: Could the garden — and Mary — grow more with a friend?

reaction.speaker: mary
reaction.text: The roses still look so grey…

options.text: Trust Dickon, and ask him to promise to keep it secret.
options.feedback: Trusting someone while respecting a promise showed respect.

reaction.speaker: dickon
reaction.text: I can keep secrets, Miss. I keep 'em for the birds' nests on the moor.

options.text: Share it, because the roses need care and help.
options.feedback: Thinking about what the garden needs showed caring.

reaction.speaker: dickon
reaction.text: Eh, Miss! Look — there's green inside this stem. It's wick!

steps.book: Mary speaks rudely to Martha because she is used to giving orders.
steps.today: Someone is rude to a cafeteria worker, a cleaner or a bus driver.

missions.title: Help Colin
missions.summary: Mary follows the sound of crying and finds Colin, a lonely boy who believes he will never get well. She learns to listen to him — and to be honest with him.
missions.stageText: The trees begin to grow new leaves.

steps.text: One stormy night, Mary hears crying somewhere in the house. She follows the sound down a long corridor, past dark portraits, to a door hidden behind a tapestry.
Inside, a thin boy lies in a huge bed. He is Colin Craven, Mr. Craven's son. He has hardly ever been outside, and he believes he will never walk.
Emotion Match: look at Colin's face, how he moves and what he says. How is he feeling?

rounds.speaker: colin
rounds.posture: Lies in bed and turns his face to the wall.
rounds.phrase: Nobody ever comes to see me.

rounds.speaker: colin
rounds.posture: Clenches his fists and shouts at the nurse.
rounds.phrase: Go away! I'll get a lump on my back and die!

rounds.speaker: colin
rounds.posture: Sits up. His eyes are bright.
rounds.phrase: Could I really see the garden one day?

steps.speaker: colin
steps.text: I don't think anyone understands how I feel.

steps.speaker: colin
steps.prompt: Colin looks away. How should Mary answer him?

options.text: “You should stop thinking like that.”
options.feedback: Think about how Colin might feel in this situation.

reaction.speaker: colin
reaction.text: That's what everyone says. Nobody listens!

options.text: “I want to understand. Tell me what happened.”
options.feedback: This choice showed understanding.

reaction.speaker: colin
reaction.text: Nobody ever asked me that before… Everyone thinks I'll die. Even Father can't bear to look at me.

options.text: “Maybe you just need to be alone.”
options.feedback: Colin is alone almost all the time. What might he need instead?

reaction.speaker: colin
reaction.text: I'm always alone.

options.text: “Let's talk about something else.”
options.feedback: Changing the subject can be kind, but Colin may feel unheard.

reaction.speaker: colin
reaction.text: …All right. What about?

steps.text: A few days later, Colin has a terrible tantrum. He screams that he can feel a lump on his back. The nurse and servants are too frightened to go in.

steps.speaker: colin
steps.prompt: Colin is screaming and scared. What should Mary do?

options.text: Calmly but firmly offer to look at his back to show him the truth.
options.feedback: Helping Colin face his fear with the truth showed caring.

reaction.speaker: colin
reaction.text: There's… no lump? Truly? Not even a tiny one?

options.text: Run away and leave him alone.
options.feedback: Colin is frightened. What could help him feel safe?

reaction.speaker: colin
reaction.text: …Everyone always goes away.

options.text: Tell the nurse he is impossible.
options.feedback: Think about what Colin is really afraid of.

reaction.speaker: colin
reaction.text: I hate everyone!

options.text: Sit with him and tell him about the garden until he calms down.
options.feedback: Staying with Colin and calming him showed compassion.

reaction.speaker: colin
reaction.text: Tell me more about the roses. Are they really waking up?

steps.book: Colin is shut away in his room and feels that nobody understands him.
steps.today: A student is left out of an online group and stops talking at school.

missions.title: Dickon's Garden
missions.summary: Dickon brings the garden back to life with patience and gentle hands. Together, the children plan how Colin can come to the garden — and stand up for him.

steps.text: Dickon Sowerby comes from the moor with a little fox, a crow and two squirrels. Animals trust him because he is always gentle and calm.

steps.speaker: dickon
steps.text: We'll need to clear the old path, Miss Mary, so Master Colin's chair can get through. Will tha' help me?
Restore the Path: put the five value stones in order, from the foundation (1) to the top (5).

steps.speaker: dickon
steps.text: Master Colin wants to come to th' garden. But he's afraid people will stare at him.

steps.speaker: dickon
steps.prompt: How should Mary and Dickon help Colin come to the garden?

options.text: Take him out quickly, even though he says he isn't ready.
options.feedback: Wanting to help is good — but how might Colin feel if he isn't ready?

reaction.speaker: colin
reaction.text: Wait! Not yet — I'm not ready!

options.text: Plan it together with Colin, and let him choose the day.
options.feedback: Letting Colin choose showed respect.

reaction.speaker: colin
reaction.text: Tomorrow. Let's go tomorrow, when the sun is out.

options.text: Invite everyone in the house to watch his first trip.
options.feedback: Colin is afraid of being stared at. How might a crowd feel to him?

reaction.speaker: colin
reaction.text: No! I won't have them staring at me!

options.text: Ask the gardeners to stay away, so he feels safe.
options.feedback: Thinking about what makes Colin feel safe showed compassion.

reaction.speaker: colin
reaction.text: Just us three? Then it will be our secret.

steps.text: Dickon pushes Colin's chair through the hidden door. Colin sees the green buds, the birds and the sky. For the first time in years, he laughs out loud.

steps.speaker: colin
steps.prompt: Old Ben Weatherstaff looks over the wall and says Colin has “crooked legs”. Colin is hurt. What should Dickon do?

options.text: Laugh along with Ben.
options.feedback: How do you think Colin felt in that moment?

reaction.speaker: colin
reaction.text: …Even here, people laugh at me.

options.text: Stand next to Colin and tell Ben that Colin is getting stronger.
options.feedback: Standing up for Colin showed compassion.

reaction.speaker: colin
reaction.text: I'm going to stand! Look, Ben — I'm standing!

options.text: Invite Ben to come in and see Colin for himself.
options.feedback: Helping Ben see the truth was kind and wise.

reaction.speaker: ben
reaction.text: Well I never… the lad's as straight as I am!

options.text: Tell Colin to just ignore it.
options.feedback: Ignoring hurtful words is hard alone. What could a friend do?

reaction.speaker: colin
reaction.text: It's easy for you to say.

steps.book: Dickon and Mary plan carefully so that Colin can enjoy the garden safely.
steps.today: A class plans a trip so that a student with a disability can join every activity.

missions.title: The Digital Garden
missions.summary: The garden turns into a digital garden. In group chats and comments, the same choices appear: to ignore, to join in, or to care.

steps.text: Colin was hidden away and felt nobody understood him. Today, people can feel the same way online. Welcome to the Digital Garden.

steps.title: Class 8B 🎒

messages.text: he's so boring 🙄 let's remove him

messages.system: Dana removed Timur from the group

steps.prompt: Your classmate is removed from the group chat. What would you do?

options.text: Ignore it.
options.feedback: Think about how Timur might feel when he sees he was removed.

result.system: Nobody says anything. Timur is still outside the group.

options.text: Add another joke: “bye Timur 👋”
options.feedback: Jokes can hurt more online, because everyone sees them. How would Timur feel?

options.text: Privately ask Timur if he's okay.
options.feedback: Checking on Timur privately showed caring.

result.text: (to Timur) hey, saw what happened. are you okay?

options.text: Ask others to stop, and add Timur back.
options.feedback: Standing up for Timur in front of everyone showed compassion.

result.text: that's not fair. he's in our class too

result.system: You added Timur to the group

steps.title: PE Class Memes
steps.prompt: Someone posts an embarrassing photo without permission. What would you do?

options.text: React with 😂
options.feedback: Every reaction makes the post bigger. How might Aliya feel?

result.system: Your reaction was added. 12 people reacted.

options.text: Forward it to another chat.
options.feedback: Sharing a photo without permission can hurt someone a lot.

result.system: The photo was shared to 1 more chat.

options.text: Tell Nurik privately to delete it — it wasn't okay.
options.feedback: Protecting Aliya's privacy showed respect.

result.text: (to Nurik) pls delete it, she didn't agree to that

options.text: Message Aliya, ask how she feels and offer to help report it.
options.feedback: Supporting Aliya directly showed caring.

result.text: (to Aliya) hey, I saw the photo. are you ok? want me to help report it?

steps.title: Dias posted a drawing 🎨

messages.text: my 5 year old brother draws better 💀

steps.prompt: A student receives rude comments. What would you do?

options.text: Like the rude comment.
options.feedback: Likes tell people the rude comment is okay. How would Dias feel?

options.text: Scroll past.
options.feedback: Scrolling past is easy, but Dias only sees the rude comments.

options.text: Write a kind comment about what you like.
options.feedback: A kind comment can balance hurtful ones. That showed kindness.

result.text: I love the colours of the tree! keep drawing 🌿

options.text: Report the comments and ask people to stop.
options.feedback: Making the space safer showed respect.

result.text: be nice, it's his first drawing

steps.title: Madi

messages.text: honestly I feel so alone lately. like nobody really gets me

steps.prompt: A friend sends you a message saying they feel alone. What would you do?

options.text: Reply “same lol”.
options.feedback: Madi shared something serious. How could you show you heard them?

options.text: Call or meet Madi, and listen.
options.feedback: Making time to really listen showed understanding.

result.text: I'm here. can I call you? I want to listen

options.text: Send a ❤️ and change the topic.
options.feedback: The heart is kind, but Madi might feel unheard.

result.text: ❤️ did you see the new episode?

options.text: Say you care, and suggest also talking to a trusted adult.
options.feedback: Caring and getting a trusted adult involved is a strong, safe choice.

result.text: I care about you. we can talk, and maybe also tell someone you trust, like a teacher?
maybe… will you come with me?

steps.note: If a friend feels alone or sad for a long time, it is always okay to tell a trusted adult.

steps.title: Science Project 🔬

messages.text: hi everyone! I'm Nurlan, I'm new 😊

steps.prompt: Everyone ignores a new student in an online group. What would you do?

options.text: Do nothing.
options.feedback: Being “seen by 17” with no replies can feel very lonely.

options.text: Reply “welcome!”
options.feedback: A warm welcome showed kindness.

options.text: Welcome him and ask what he likes.
options.feedback: Being curious about Nurlan showed understanding.

result.text: welcome! what kind of science do you like?

options.text: Invite him into your project team.
options.feedback: Making room for Nurlan in your team showed caring.

result.text: Nurlan, want to join our team? we need one more

steps.book: Colin is hidden away. Few people visit or talk to him, and he feels forgotten.
steps.today: A classmate is removed from a group chat, and nobody says anything.
